source: Standard posing vocabulary taught across portrait/editorial photography courses (weight shift, S-curve, forced perspective, triangle grouping, catch-in-motion candids) - not one course's material specifically, the same broad-vocabulary approach prompt_bank.json's own core/camera/lens layers already take.
note: Posing is descriptive spec content, like wardrobe/setting/mood - it is NOT one of realism_lint.py's 8 gated photorealism layers, so nothing here needs a DETECT keyword. A pose (picked or typed) is the recommended base; `techniques` stack on top, additive and opt-in. None of it is individually required - a lone technique stack or a single free-text phrase composes on its own, only a wholly empty request is refused. No conflicts list: one pose is picked at a time and no technique fights a pose or another technique.

weight-back-leg.label: Weight on the back leg
weight-back-leg.phrase: weight shifted onto the back leg, the front knee softly bent
weight-back-leg.note: The default flattering stance - avoids the flat, evenly-weighted look of standing straight at the camera.

chin-forward-down.label: Chin forward and down
chin-forward-down.phrase: chin brought slightly forward and down to elongate the neckline
chin-forward-down.note: Fights the double-chin/foreshortened-neck look a straight-on chin produces at most focal lengths.

three-quarter-turn.label: Three-quarter turn
three-quarter-turn.phrase: body turned three-quarters toward camera rather than square to it
three-quarter-turn.note: Reads slimmer and more dynamic than a fully square-to-camera stance.

hand-near-jaw.label: Hand near the jaw
hand-near-jaw.phrase: a hand resting lightly near the jawline rather than flat against the cheek
hand-near-jaw.note: Flat-against-the-cheek reads as posed and stiff; near the jaw, fingers relaxed, reads natural.

s-curve.label: S-curve spine
s-curve.phrase: an elongated S-curve through the spine and hips
s-curve.note: The classic fashion-editorial line - shoulders and hips angled opposite each other.

forced-perspective.label: Forced perspective
forced-perspective.phrase: a limb extended toward the lens for forced perspective
forced-perspective.note: Exaggerates scale and adds dynamism - needs a wider lens to read correctly, pairs oddly with a long telephoto.

asymmetrical-stance.label: Asymmetrical stance
asymmetrical-stance.phrase: an off-balance, asymmetrical stance rather than a centred, even one
asymmetrical-stance.note: Deliberate imbalance is what separates an editorial pose from a catalogue one.

forward-lean.label: Slight forward lean
forward-lean.phrase: a slight forward lean toward the camera
forward-lean.note: Reads as engaged and confident rather than passive - the default corporate-headshot instruction.

shoulders-angled.label: Shoulders angled off-axis
shoulders-angled.phrase: shoulders angled away from the camera axis while the face turns back toward it
shoulders-angled.note: Avoids the mugshot look of shoulders and face both square to the lens.

genuine-microexpression.label: Genuine micro-expression
genuine-microexpression.phrase: a genuine, soft-eyed micro-expression rather than a held, frozen smile
genuine-microexpression.note: A held smile reads dead in the eyes past a few seconds - the real thing this note is fighting is the AI model's tendency toward a flat, identical grin.

staggered-heights.label: Staggered heights
staggered-heights.phrase: heights staggered front-to-back rather than lined up flat
staggered-heights.note: A flat line of equal heights is the single most common amateur group-photo mistake.

triangle-arrangement.label: Triangle arrangement
triangle-arrangement.phrase: the group arranged in a triangle rather than a straight line
triangle-arrangement.note: Same logic as the composition bank's own triangle guide, applied to bodies instead of frame geometry.

genuine-interaction.label: Genuine interaction
genuine-interaction.phrase: genuine interaction between the group rather than everyone facing camera
genuine-interaction.note: Not everyone has to look at the lens - some heads turned toward each other reads far less staged.

mid-gesture.label: Caught mid-gesture
mid-gesture.phrase: caught mid-gesture rather than posed and still
mid-gesture.note: The core of what makes a candid read as candid - motion frozen partway, not a held pose.

walking-mid-stride.label: Walking, mid-stride
walking-mid-stride.note: A specific, reliable candid: mid-stride avoids both feet flat on the ground, which reads as posed.

natural-reaction.label: Natural reaction
natural-reaction.phrase: a natural laugh or reaction caught in the moment
natural-reaction.note: Genuine reaction beats a directed expression for anything meant to read as unposed.

asymmetrical-weight.label: Asymmetrical weight distribution
asymmetrical-weight.phrase: weight distributed asymmetrically across the body, not perfectly even
asymmetrical-weight.note: Perfectly even weight distribution is a small, reliable tell of a posed-and-held shot rather than a lived-in moment.

relaxed-hands.label: Relaxed hands
relaxed-hands.phrase: hands relaxed and loose, fingers gently curved rather than clenched or pressed flat
relaxed-hands.note: Clenched or flat-pressed hands are one of the most common AI-generated-hand tells this app can actually fight with wording.

soft-eyed-expression.label: Soft-eyed expression
soft-eyed-expression.phrase: a soft, genuine expression in the eyes rather than a fixed stare
soft-eyed-expression.note: Distinct from `genuine-microexpression` above (a pose-specific note) - this is a general, stackable instruction usable with any pose.

negative-space-limbs.label: Negative space between limbs and torso
negative-space-limbs.phrase: visible negative space kept between the arms and the torso
negative-space-limbs.note: Arms pressed flat against the body reads stiff and widens the silhouette - a small gap reads relaxed and more flattering.

relaxed-posture.label: Relaxed posture
relaxed-posture.phrase: a relaxed, natural breathing posture, not held rigid
relaxed-posture.note: A held-rigid pose is what makes an otherwise good pose still read as posed - this is the instruction that undoes that.
